name: Motomachi
tagline: The slope district with the Western buildings
description: The hillside below Mount Hakodate, where the consulates, churches and merchant houses built after the port opened to foreign trade in 1854 still stand along steep cobbled slopes. The Russian Orthodox church and the old public hall are the landmarks.
bestFor: Anyone here for the architecture and the views
pros: The most atmospheric district in the city
Ropeway to the night view at the top
Views down the slopes to the harbour
cons: Steep slopes, punishing in winter ice
Busy with tour groups in season

name: Hakodate Station and the Morning Market
tagline: The transport hub and the squid
description: The area around the station, with the morning market where the squid comes out of the tank in front of you, the ferry terminal nearby and the tram lines converging. It is the most practical base in the city and the cheapest for hotels.
bestFor: Short stays and anyone moving around Hokkaido by train
pros: Trains, trams and the morning market at the door
Widest hotel choice at fair prices
cons: The market winds down by early afternoon
Some blocks are tired and empty

name: Goryokaku
tagline: The star fort and the city's actual centre of gravity
description: The area around the star-shaped fort built in 1857, whose moat is lined with cherry trees and whose tower gives the best view of the shape. This is where modern Hakodate shops and eats, with the largest concentration of everyday life in the city.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting supermarkets, shops and ordinary life
pros: Where the city actually shops and eats
The fort and its cherry trees in May
cons: Twenty minutes by tram from the harbour

name: Yunokawa Onsen
tagline: The hot spring quarter on the eastern shore
description: A hot spring district on the coast east of the centre, one of Hokkaido's oldest, with ryokan and hotels along the shore and public baths including a footbath at the tram terminus. The monkeys at the tropical botanical garden bathe here in winter.
bestFor: Anyone who wants a hot spring at the end of the working day
pros: Hot spring baths throughout the district
Tram terminus connects to the whole city

name: Nanae and Onuma
tagline: The lakes and the volcano half an hour north
description: The area around Onuma Quasi-National Park, where a cluster of lakes and islets sits beneath Mount Komagatake, half an hour by train from the city. It is where Hakodate goes for cycling, canoeing and, in winter, the frozen lake.
bestFor: Anyone prioritising the outdoors over the city
pros: Lakes, cycling and canoeing at the door
cons: Half an hour from the city
